programmes.d: A twelve-year-old girl claimed she had been abducted and sexually assaulted. She recounted what happened in such a flat, unemotional voice that police found it difficult to believe her. Fibers on her clothing would prove she was telling the truth.
A bomb kills a man and a painstaking search yields tiny clues which precisely identify the killer.
Respected surgeon is stabbed to death. However the key suspect has a solid alibi.

The body of a wealthy American businessman was found in his rental car. Teeth and bone fragments were the only remains. When the victim's wife files an insurance claim for $7 million, investigators seek the help of a renowned forensic anthropologist.
Forensic developments reveal new facts in the case of a man convicted of sexual assault.

When an elderly couple died in a suspicious house fire, their son became the prime suspect. Investigators turned to forensic science to determine if the fire had been set deliberately, or if it was an unfortunate accident.
Blood splatter is found in the bedroom of a missing girl's boyfriend.
After shooting his victims in the head, the killer staged the scene, placed the incriminating evidence into a plastic bag and tossed it into the river.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica.
The only clue recovered from a shooting is a twelve-guage shotgun. Scientists use unique methods to lift the serial number from the weapon to trace it to its owner
In 2001, Ginger Hayes and her infant son Nicholas were abducted during a carjacking.

Three seemingly unrelated deaths prove to be serial murders. The killer had been careful; he used poison which had no taste or odor. Fortunately for investigators, it also had a unique chemical signature.
On the night of May 22, 1992, Betty Wilson discovered her husband lying in a pool of blood.
When a woman and her daughter didn't return home from shopping, her husband directed police to a nearby mall. The child's body was found, but there was no sign of the wife.
Scientific evidence casts new light on a 10-year-old disappearance.
For six years, a serial killer prowled the streets of New York City. He wrote letters to police and The New York Post, indicating he would kill twelve people — one for each astrological sign.
Car with three agents collides with deputy's car; investigations find two different conclusions.
When an off-duty policeman was shot dead, his fellow officers were determined to solve the crime. They needed clues to find the killer and they discovered them in tiny fibres and an asthma inhaler.
A jeweler's search through old sales records helps police find likely suspects in a couple's murder.
On the night of May 22, 1992, Betty Wilson returned home after a meeting and discovered her husband lying in a pool of blood. Jack Wilson had obviously been murdered — but how?
A flight attendant's brutal murder prompts the son of another victim to contact the police.

Soon after organizing a workers' strike, a union official is executed in his home. Neither his wife nor anyone in the neighborhood hear any gunshots. It takes a forensic sound test, an electron microscope and a nightgown to explain why.
A nosy neighbor with a disturbing obsession becomes a suspect in a woman's murder.
In 1997, Kelly Eckart's car was found, with her belongings still in it, after she worked a late shift in Franklin, Indiana. Days later, her body was found in an isolated ravine.
How did the stalker obtain the security system code for his victim's home? Police needed answers.

Police suspect Dr. John "Jack" Boyle in the disappearance of his wife, Noreen, when he signs mortgage papers for a new house with a woman pretending to be his spouse. The police later find Noreen's body in the basement of Dr. Boyle's new house.
A convenience store security camera captures footage of an employee's murder.

When a young woman disappeared, police feared she was the latest victim in a string of similar crimes. A pair of bloody gloves, unique tire tracks and ordinary pine needles provided investigators with some extraordinary clues.
A hairdresser was murdered. But the evidence at the crime scene didn't match any of the suspects.
When a hit-and-run accident claimed the life of a high school athlete, everyone in town mourned his passing. Finding the killer was a long shot at best.
When two women from the same town were murdered, police feared a serial killer was on the loose.

An obstetrician returned home from the hospital and found his wife on the bathroom floor. She was covered with blood and not breathing. He tried unsuccessfully to revive her, staining his clothes with her blood in the process.
Police are led on a wild goose chase when the wife of a prominent banker is kidnapped.

When two women from the same town were murdered in the same way, police feared a serial killer was on the loose. At first they thought the victims had nothing in common until they found tiny clues linking them to the same man.
Two people in Seattle, Washington died after taking an over-the-counter pain reliever.
When the number and volume of bloodstains at the scene was greater than usual, it was up to forensic scientists to find out why.
A married couple went on a mini-vacation in Key West. But the wife went missing.

When the wife of a well-known dentist is found dead, police struggle to identify a suspect. Some fibers and a study of the weather patterns on the night of the murder break the case open and reveal the killer.
A dismembered body is dumped on the side of the New Jersey Turnpike.
When a heart surgeon is found dead, investigators uncover his new wife's history of violence.

When Genell Plude is found dead in her bathroom, the scene points to suicide. But a coroner's inquest and a unique application of forensic science give investigators a different explanation for her death.
A woman disappears without a trace. Even though foul play is suspected, the leads don't pan out.

In 2002, a small community in upstate New York was devastated when Patty Wlasiuk died in a truck accident. But burdock seed pods found in her hair and on her clothes indicated that this was no accident — it was cold-blooded murder.
Series premiere. A flight attendant went missing and was never seen again.
When 19-year-old Lori Auker left her Pennsylvania home for work and never arrived, it took space-age technology, cat hairs and insects to pinpoint the woman's abductor.

In the search for the killer of two Texas teenagers, a behavioral profile led to suspect Jason Massey. Hard science proved the profile was correct, and Massey was executed by lethal injection on April 3, 2001.
When hunters found a skull in a Texas canyon, a forensic artist was able to reconstruct her face.
A flawed envelope is an unlikely clue to identifying a killer who laced a water cooler with cyanide.

In 1993, young mother Tammy Tatum was sexually assaulted and murdered in her Longmont, Colorado apartment. Police initially suspected her estranged husband, but did not have enough evidence to charge him and the case went cold.
A wealthy man and his wife were attacked by three masked men outside their luxurious Louisiana home.
The body of 16-year-old Leanne Tiernan was discovered nine months after she disappeared. Forensic scientists found clues that painted a virtual portrait of her killer.
In a 1992 murder case, the autopsy of a cremated body turns up telltale clues of foul play.

Janice Johnson was found dead at the foot of her basement stairs. Police in Nova Scotia had to unravel the circumstances surrounding Janice's death and answer the question: Was it an accident or murder?
During a Christmas party, a young girl disappeared and forensic science is used to solve the case.

When a wealthy real estate tycoon goes missing, it appears to be foul play. In his will, he leaves instructions in case he should die under violent circumstances — which were carried out after a hiker comes across his bullet-ridden skull.
When a little girl got sick and died, investigators were stumped. Was it an accident or murder?
A security guard disappeared from his post without a trace; his remains were found a year later in a remote campsite.
When a woman exhibits flu-like symptoms before dying, investigators determine she was poisoned.
Young Navajos in the Southwest were dying at an alarming rate. The tribe's medicine men provided investigators with a critical clue that would lead halfway around the world to a most unlikely killer.
A lifelong resident in a Tasmania town was murdered. Robbery appeared to be the motive.

After a day of fishing in a quiet village in Switzerland, a teenage boy doesn't return home as planned. The investigation reveals some important microscopic evidence in the water near where he was last seen.
In 1981, New York correctional officer Donna Payant disappeared and was later found in a landfill.
When 19-year-old Lori Auker left her Pennsylvania home for work and never arrived, it took space-age technology, cat hairs and insects to pinpoint the woman's abductor.
Naval officer threatening to go public about sexual harassment and assault at work is murdered.
In the 1980s, a trio of unsolved murders occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas. Later, a fourth murder from the same time period provided the police with far more than they realized.
A beautiful young woman falls to her death from a cliff overlooking the ocean.

On September 17, 1984, in a suburb of Tucson, Arizona, eight-year-old Vicki Hoskins left home on her pink bicycle to mail a letter for her mother. She never returned, but her slightly damaged bicycle was found nearby.
A hamburger bun provides the key to solving the case of a young woman murdered in her bathtub.
Tracey Frame, 35, was convicted of killing David Nixon in April 2002 after he planned to end their relationship.
Woman's apparent suicide proves to be murder when a hidden note is found in her china cabinet.

When police discovered the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife, authorities linked 20 cat hairs found on her jacket to a cat owned by Beamish's parents. It was the first time animal DNA was used to solve a criminal case.
Garbage bag leads to a killer.
The bodies of several women are found on a remote hill in California. The police get a break when a prostitute escapes and is able to identify her attacker and his automobile.
Police investigate a discarded sleeping bag containing bloody sneakers and a purse.

The body of a young woman was found a mile from her abandoned car. Police were especially concerned when they realized the victim had come to them for protection just two weeks earlier after a road rage incident.
A woman is killed weeks before testifying against the man who sexually assaulted her.
When a dry cleaner employee is raped and murdered in her store, police turn to forensic science for the answers they need.
Police use DNA profiles of seed pods from a truck to catch a killer.
In 1986, Gary Dale Larson was stabbed to death in his Edmond, Oklahoma home. The killer then sexually assaulted Larson's girlfriend, Janet Haynes.
Two people in Seattle, Washington died after taking an over-the-counter pain reliever.
On Halloween night 2004, Adriane Insogna and Leslie Mazzara were brutally murdered in their Napa, California home.
A young woman suddenly becomes critically ill, eventually leaving her unable to walk.
At the scene of a vicious murder, the killer went to a great deal of effort to wipe away his fingerprints and obscure his shoe impressions left when he tracked blood trails on the floor.
Car with three agents collides with deputy's car; investigations find two different conclusions.
Chilling tale of debt and deceit when the head chef of a restaurant is found dead.

A 29-year-old woman is killed instantly when a bomb explodes in her home. The device is so powerful that it embedded shrapnel in houses across the street. The bomber had not only knowledge and skill, but also a motive for murder.
A woman is found dead from a gunshot wound and police suspect her husband.

When police find the body of 11-year-old Krista Harrison, there are few clues to the killer's identity. But authorities are intrigued by unusual orange fibers embedded in clothing found near the victim.
Clues at the scene of a possible murder-suicide lead investigators to believe otherwise.

California police had several suspects in the robbery and brutal murder of an elderly couple. Ten years later, a determined forensic scientist used material from a dentist's office to uncover ballistic evidence that had been overlooked.
Further investigation proves that a woman's suffocation after falling asleep was staged.

In 1991, San Francisco pornographer Artie Mitchell was murdered in his home. His brother and business partner, who was found near the scene carrying a rifle, later confesses to shooting Artie.The question is whether the shooting was premeditated.
A physics professor and NASA technology help to catch a killer.
A retired police officer is found dead with a single gunshot wound to the head. His wife says the motive was robbery, but later tells police he committed suicide.
Armed with little else, police hoped that shoe impressions found at a Lansing, Michigan crime scene would put their investigation of Audrey Nichols' murder back on track.
An abandoned, still-running car leads investigators to a body with unusual marks.
The use of DNA testing helps exonerate a person accused of raping a young Virginia woman.

When an 11-year-old girl disappears from a remote Alaska town, investigators wonder if she has been attacked by a bear or become lost in the dense woods. Eventually, they realize that neither assumption is true.
In a 1992 murder case, the autopsy of a cremated body turns up telltale clues of foul play.

A beautiful young woman falls to her death from a cliff overlooking the ocean. Initially, investigators think it was a tragic accident. But after a forensic examination, police uncover a very different picture of what happened.
